claim: Table 6.5.3.1-1 imposes no requirement of its own. It is a correspondence map. Neither its caption nor any cell contains shall, should or will, and it has no Type, Usage or R/O/C column.
value: Caption verbatim: Table 6.5.3.1-1: Corresponding Algorithm Identification Attributes and Content Items. The only sentence invoking it, at Vol 3 Section 6.5.3.1, printed page 81 IHE line 1744 continuing onto page 82, reads: In SR instances, when an algorithm is identified in the SR Tree (typically in TID 4019 and/or TID 1004) it will also be identified in the Contributing Equipment Sequence (0018,A001). The content items, if present, shall contain the same value as the corresponding attribute shown in Table 6.5.3.1-1. Force: will for the co-identification expectation, then shall for value equality, gated by the scope clause In SR instances and by the condition if present

dropped: nothing. Both occurrences of the string 6.5.3.1-1 in the document were read. The second, at Vol 1 Open and Closed Issues printed page 16 question 26, uses can and describes the table as correspondences, so it is non-normative
external_source: IHE RAD TF Supplement AI Results (AIR) Rev 1.3, Vol 3, Section 6.5.3.1 and Table 6.5.3.1-1, printed pages 81 to 82
status_note: One ambiguity is reported and deliberately not resolved. The invoking sentence says the corresponding attribute, singular, while the table has two attribute columns: column 1, a Contributing Equipment Sequence attribute, and column 4, an Algorithm Identification Sequence attribute. The sentence does not say which. Its scope clause is In SR instances and its subject is The content items, while column 4 is introduced by the paragraph after the table, which begins In some non-SR instances. Whether the equality obligation reaches column 4 is not stated in the document and this study does not decide it.
notes: The value equality shall constrains what a content item contains, never whether it exists. AIR still cannot be cited as requiring TID 1004 or TID 4019 content items to be present. That part of STD-06 stands unchanged.

claim: Table 6.5.3.1-1 adds no requirement beyond the unconditional Creator shall already recorded at STD-06, so claim 3 gains no new yardstick from it and continues to rest on PS3.3 Type 1 requirements, with AIR cited as a secondary yardstick through Section 6.5.3.1 alone.
value: Required of the Creator by the table: nothing. Merely mapped: the TID 1004 Device Observer content items, the TID 4019 Algorithm Identification content items, and Algorithm Source (0024,0202), Algorithm Name (0066,0036) and Algorithm Version (0066,0031) of the Algorithm Identification Macro
floor: not applicable, this row resolves a citation rather than quoting a rate
external_source: IHE RAD TF Supplement AI Results (AIR) Rev 1.3, Vol 3, Table 6.5.3.1-1
status_note: This closes the question the track was opened to settle. The hoped for outcome was a citable AIR yardstick over the algorithm identification attributes. There is none. The table is a map, and the manuscript must cite it as intent rather than as a requirement.
notes: Claim 3's measurable yardsticks remain the four Type 1 Enhanced General Equipment attributes at STD-04 and the Type 1 children of a present SegmentationAlgorithmIdentificationSequence at STD-03.

section_title: IHE AIR Table 6.5.3.1-1, read from the PDF
claim: The four column grid of Table 6.5.3.1-1, previously reconstructed from layout-preserving text and flagged as never visually confirmed, is now confirmed. One widely used extraction mode reads the table wrongly and its reading is recorded so it cannot be reintroduced.
value: Four readings agree: pdftotext -table, pdftotext -lineprinter, the page's own ruling-line geometry, and a visual render in the Chrome PDF viewer. pdftotext -layout disagrees: it places (121012, DCM, Device Observer UID) on the Software Versions row. The geometry puts that run's baselines at y 493.44 and y 483.11, inside the Device UID row band of y 476.52 to 506.04, and the render agrees. The layout reading is an artifact of unequal cell text heights
